title: Compact the Memories workbench filter and detail layout
description:
Problem: the live `/memories` review showed the filter command bar, pagination, metadata chips, nested content scroller, and references section competing for a small viewport. The search controls take roughly the first quarter of the visible page, the results list can show only a small slice, and the selected memory body has limited reading space before another nested reference scroller appears.

Desired outcome: Memories remains information-dense, but the selected record body and search results get more of the first viewport.

Scope:
- In scope: compact/collapsible advanced filters, tighter search-mode controls, denser pagination, metadata chip grouping, references folding, and clearer result/detail pane proportions.
- Out of scope: changing memory search semantics or record schema.

Acceptance criteria:
- At narrow widths, a selected memory shows materially more body content without hiding critical commands.
- Basic search remains immediately available; secondary filters can collapse or move behind an advanced-controls affordance.
- References and dense metadata can be expanded, copied, or navigated without permanently taking priority over body text.
- No horizontal overflow or nested-scroll confusion is introduced.

Validation:
- Capture before/after `/memories` screenshots at narrow and desktop widths.
- Re-run route-smoke or focused browser checks for search, result selection, pagination, and reference navigation.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from 2026-05-25 live visual review: `/memories` used a tall filter stack and nested detail/reference scrolling that limited the selected memory reading area.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Completed the `/memories` layout compaction: basic search stays visible, `Search options` now collapses status/tags/mode controls, related context folds behind a summary row, and the selected-memory link grid no longer uses a nested capped scroller. Focused guard `MemoryViewerMarkup_CollapsesSecondaryFiltersAndRelatedContextByDefault` passed in `MemorySmith.Tests/TagGovernanceTests.cs`. Browser verification on `http://127.0.0.1:5124/memories` confirmed collapsed default panels at 760px, expanding `Search options` and `Related context`, lexical search for `Historical Validation Baseline Alias`, pagination from page 1 to page 2, and related-memory navigation to `Admin Configuration Surface Current State`. Screenshots: `artifacts/browser-validation/tsk-0124/20260526-135259-interactive/`.
